questiontext.text: Which C++ feature is the classic example of ad-hoc polymorphism?

answer.text: Function and operator overloading

feedback.text: Correct — overloading is ad-hoc polymorphism.

answer.text: Virtual functions dispatched through a vtable

feedback.text: No — that is runtime (subtype) polymorphism.

answer.text: Templates instantiated per type

feedback.text: No — that is parametric polymorphism.

answer.text: Public inheritance forming an is-a hierarchy

feedback.text: No — inheritance is not ad-hoc polymorphism.

generalfeedback.text: Ad-hoc polymorphism is overloading: the same name behaves differently depending on the argument types.

questiontext.text: What must differ between two overloaded functions that share the same name?

answer.text: Their parameter types and/or number of parameters

feedback.text: Correct — the parameter list distinguishes overloads.

answer.text: Only their return type

feedback.text: No — return type alone cannot distinguish overloads.

answer.text: Only the names of their parameters

feedback.text: No — parameter names are irrelevant to overload resolution.

answer.text: Nothing; identical signatures are allowed

feedback.text: No — two identical signatures would be a redefinition error.

generalfeedback.text: Overloads share a name but differ in the parameter list (types and/or count); return type alone is not enough.

questiontext.text: When does the compiler decide which overloaded function to call?

answer.text: At compile time, via overload resolution (static dispatch)

feedback.text: Correct — overloading is resolved statically.

answer.text: At run time, via the vtable

feedback.text: No — that is dynamic dispatch for virtual functions.

answer.text: At link time, by the linker matching symbols

feedback.text: No — overload resolution happens during compilation.

answer.text: At install time, by the package manager

feedback.text: No — that has nothing to do with overload resolution.

generalfeedback.text: Overload resolution is performed by the compiler at compile time (static dispatch), based on argument types.

questiontext.text: Defining operator+ for your own class is an example of what?

answer.text: Operator overloading — a form of ad-hoc polymorphism

feedback.text: Correct — the same operator symbol gains new meaning for your type.

answer.text: Runtime polymorphism via virtual dispatch

feedback.text: No — operator overloading is resolved at compile time.

answer.text: Template instantiation

feedback.text: No — no template parameter is involved here.

answer.text: Private inheritance

feedback.text: No — that is unrelated to operators.

generalfeedback.text: Operator overloading lets an operator symbol take on type-specific behavior, resolved at compile time.

questiontext.text: Which statements about ad-hoc polymorphism (overloading) are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Overloads share a name but differ in parameter types or count

feedback.text: Yes — the parameter list distinguishes them.

answer.text: It is resolved at compile time (static dispatch)

feedback.text: Yes — the compiler picks the overload.

answer.text: It is resolved at run time through the vtable

feedback.text: No — that describes runtime polymorphism, not overloading.

answer.text: Two functions can be overloaded solely by return type

feedback.text: No — differing only in return type is not a valid overload.

generalfeedback.text: Overloading distinguishes functions by their parameter list and is resolved statically at compile time.

questiontext.text: Overload resolution for function overloading happens at compile time.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: Correct — overloading uses static (compile-time) dispatch.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Overloading is indeed resolved by the compiler at compile time.

questiontext.text: Two functions with the same name and parameters but different return types form a valid overload set.

answer.text: true

feedback.text: No — differing only in return type is not allowed.

answer.text: false

feedback.text: Correct — overloads must differ in their parameter list, not just the return type.

questiontext.text: Giving several functions the same name with different parameter lists is called function ______.

answer.text: overloading

feedback.text: Correct — function overloading.

answer.text: overload*

feedback.text: Correct.
